answer:
Verdict: bug found

Line 34: `pthread_cond_signal(&oven_cond);`

| Step | Thread A | Thread B | Shared state |
|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | lock(oven_mutex) succeeds |  | oven_mutex=A, pizzas_baking=1 |
| 2 | while(pizzas_baking>=3) false |  | oven_mutex=A, pizzas_baking=1 |
| 3 | unlock(oven_mutex) |  | oven_mutex=free |
| 4 | lock(oven_mutex) succeeds |  | oven_mutex=A, pizzas_baking=0 |
| 5 | unlock(oven_mutex) |  | oven_mutex=free |
| 6 | lock(oven_mutex) succeeds |  | oven_mutex=A, pizzas_baking=1 |
| 7 | while(pizzas_baking>=3) false |  | oven_mutex=A, pizzas_baking=1 |
| 8 | unlock(oven_mutex) |  | oven_mutex=free |

The baker that removes the last pizza should signal the oven_cond before releasing the mutex. Without that, the next baker cannot acquire the oven_mutex and cannot enter its while loop.

Fix the minimal diff:
```diff
--- prog.c
+++ prog.c (fixed)
@@ -32,7 +32,7 @@
     pthread_mutex_lock(&oven_mutex);
     pizzas_baking--;
     printf("Baker %d took a pizza out. Baking: %d\n", id, pizzas_baking);
-    pthread_cond_signal(&oven_cond);
+    pthread_cond_signal(&oven_cond);
     pthread_mutex_unlock(&oven_mutex);
 
     return NULL;
```

The signal happens after the unlock, so the waiter can acquire the mutex and enter its while loop. The while loop condition is checked before the critical section, so the baker can remove a pizza only when there is room.
